candidate_facts.text: The Korean War began on June 25, 1950.
North Korea invaded South Korea across the 38th parallel.
North Korea aimed to reunite the peninsula under communist rule by force.
The Korean War ended with an armistice signed on July 27, 1953.
The armistice was not a formal peace treaty.
The two Koreas remain technically at war.
The Korean Peninsula remains divided along the 38th parallel.
The 38th parallel has been maintained since the war.
The 38th parallel continues to serve as a boundary between North and South Korea.
The Korean War led to the creation of a demilitarized zone (DMZ) along the 38th parallel.
The DMZ remains heavily fortified and actively monitored.
The Korean War caused massive civilian and military casualties.
Estimates suggest over two million Korean deaths due to the Korean War.
Up to 20% of the Korean population was lost due to war or starvation.
